audit_findings.title: Current shares and leverage are paired with pre-leverage interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $655.0 million from $365.0 million at 2025 year-end to $1.020 billion at June 2026; H1 2026 interest expense was $18.075 million, $11.850 million above H1 2025, equivalent to $8.651 million after the filed 27.0% FY2025 tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: Current debt-funded share repurchases reduce the share denominator, while the FY2025 OE numerator contains interest expense from the earlier, less-leveraged capital structure.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense increased $14.4 million, or 207.8%, to $21.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $7.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to higher borrowings on our senior unsecured bank revolving credit facility (“Credit Facility”).
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: H1 2026 repurchases cost $520.0 million, shares outstanding fell from 30.864 million to 27.711 million, and debt rose $655.0 million. The computed $8.651 million after-tax H1 interest increase exceeds the approximately $8.1 million anchor-OE reduction that would eliminate the bull case's $4.69-per-share premium over the $151.70 market price. A full normalized annual adjustment remains unresolved, but the filed interim amounts are already reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate equity-level OE using normalized after-tax interest and facility fees on the June 2026 revolving debt and term loan, retain the 28.500202 million fully diluted share count, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Forgivable-loan funding may be recurring compensation omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 grants of $296.741 million less repayments of $40.110 million produced $256.631 million of net funding, $183.029 million above the $73.602 million amortization expense; reported free cash flow was $93.601 million
audit_findings.mechanism: OE appears to recognize accounting amortization but not necessarily the recurring cash investment in employee notes required to recruit and retain revenue-producing professionals.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to continue issuing unsecured general recourse forgivable loans.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-versus-expense gap is demonstrated and equals 70.7% of the $259.0 million OE anchor; net note funding also exceeded reported free cash flow by $163.030 million. The filing says these awards are significant and expected to continue, so omission of normalized funding could materially overstate distributable OE. The permanent annual burden is not established because grants, repayments, forfeitures and forgiveness vary across the retention cycle.
audit_findings.action: Trace every employee-note item in the OE calculation, build a representative multi-year schedule of grants, repayments, forgiveness and amortization, determine the normalized required net cash funding, and rerun all scenarios without double counting compensation expense.

audit_findings.title: Forgivable-loan interest can create noncash operating income
audit_findings.mechanism: Accrued employee-note interest reduces operating expenses and therefore raises OE even when that interest is expected to be forgiven; it is not captured by a purge limited to non-operating portfolio interest.
audit_findings.evidence: We record accrued interest income as a reduction to operating expenses on our Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting mechanism and likely inclusion in operating earnings are demonstrated, but neither the accrued-interest amount nor the portion ultimately forgiven is disclosed. It may overstate OE, yet the record cannot establish materiality independently of the larger forgivable-loan funding adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain annual accrued employee-note interest by OE year, identify amounts collected versus forgiven, remove the after-tax noncash portion from OE, and reconcile the adjustment against the normalized loan-funding calculation to prevent double counting.

audit_findings.title: Undisclosed legal-settlement gains may inflate the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring gain recorded as reduced SG&A raises FY2025 operating income and any OE anchor derived from it, causing the DCF to capitalize the gain through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease was partially offset by higher revenues and lower selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses, which include legal settlement gains.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence and nonrecurrence of legal-settlement gains are demonstrated: the 2026 filing says a prior-year settlement gain did not recur. However, the gain amount and its treatment in the supplied OE are undisclosed. Materiality therefore remains unresolved, although only about an $8.1 million reduction in anchor OE would remove the bull case's premium to the $151.70 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the settlement proceeds, related legal costs, tax treatment and OE workpaper classification; remove the net nonrecurring after-tax amount if retained, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The uncommenced London lease is absent from both liabilities and current rent expense
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $115.0 million of aggregate fixed rent beginning in February 2028
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental future rent and fit-out capital would reduce forecast OE or growth, but replacement rent could offset some or all of the burden.
audit_findings.evidence: The Leases are not included within “Operating lease assets” and “Operating lease liabilities” on the Consolidated Balance Sheets as of December 31, 2025, as the Company does not yet have the right to use the premises.
audit_findings.explanation: The lease is a disclosed future commitment that had not commenced and therefore was properly absent from both the historical OE anchor and recorded lease liabilities. Its valuation effect cannot be determined until existing London lease expirations, overlapping occupancy, incentives and fit-out requirements are known. It is forward-looking rather than a demonstrated error in current numbers.
audit_findings.action: Before the 2028 rent commencement, map the new leases against terminating London leases, quantify rent overlap, incentives and required fit-out capital, and rerun the forecast for only the net incremental occupancy burden.
